It looks like Billy Joel, with a bushy mustache and shaggy hair. It sounds like Billy Joel, too, with a distinctly Long Island accent. It even moves a bit like Billy Joel, smiling slightly, nodding his head and blinking.

But is it actually him?

The answer is complicated, at least in relation to a new AI-enhanced documentary, "1971: Billy Joel’s Lost Interview." Its director, Adam Ripp, obtained a long-lost radio interview with Joel, edited it down, then put the words into the mouth of a lifelike Joel generated with artificial intelligence. 

The result might be called part fact and part fiction, or perhaps science-fiction. Audiences will be able to judge for themselves when the film holds its world premiere on September 25 at the Long Island Music and Entertainment Hall of Fame in Stony Brook.

More here: https://t.co/w9JKFACplh

Ask today's best image model to draw your Q3 revenue chart and you'll get a gorgeous lie — right colors, wrong numbers, proportions that mean nothing. @F13hq just emerged from stealth with $5M in pre-seed to make models that don't do that, co-led by @CredoVentures and @PointNineCap.

@gpjanik and Ingimar Tomasson aren't building another pixel generator. They're training foundation models for vector graphics — the format where every line knows what it is. Charts that preserve the data behind them. Scientific diagrams with correct proportions. Brand layouts that follow the design system instead of hallucinating around it. Outputs stay editable and scalable, so you iterate on the design instead of re-rolling the dice.

Janik's framing: 'We didn't want to build another model that's impressively expressive and quietly wrong.' He's a serial founder who walked away from degrees in mathematics and physics — and he raised this round, per Tech Funding News, without a pitch deck. The capital goes to bringing the first model to market, plus compute, data, and hiring for more complex design tasks. Early access is already open through a developer API and a web platform.

Their claim (methodology unpublished): internal testing shows F13 beating models from the major labs on clarity, style, and precision for vector work. @Carles_Reina of Baobab Ventures and Jack Richardson of Mainframe joined as angels.

The two firms caught the same insight: the next frontier of generative AI isn't more beautiful pixels, it's models that understand two-dimensional space and tell the truth about it. That's a good bet to have on your card.

Congrats Gregory, Ingimar, and the entire F13 team. 

Up and to the right my friends! 💥🚀💪
